items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The drummer was a fellow named Yank Porter who had worked a long time at the Harlem club and I had known him for years... Yank accompanied them on drums... Yank also accompanied her with wire brushes... So Yank's brushing style was nice for the band

ctx.x: I liked working in big orchestras because of the harmonious sounds of the different sections working together and especially with three trumpets cutting riffs through an arrangement like a knife cutting through a tender steak, but I had a desire to work with a small group in a club, which was something I had not done before, so I gave my notice to Benny and joined Teddy.

The drummer was a fellow named Yank Porter who had worked a long time at the Harlem club and I had known him for years. Benny Morton was the trombonist, Jimmie Hamilton, a clarinetist whom I didn't know before, and Al Hall, whom I had seen in Teddy's big band, was the bass player.

This club, which was actually called Cafe Society Downtown, was at Sheridan Square and was owned by a man named Barney Josephson. The manager was Harold Johnson and a great barman called Lew. I will mention why Lew was a great barman to me later. There were four acts in the show and I know that three of them were discovered by and sponsored by John Hammond.
